source_text: Οὗτοι δέ γέ φασιν πολλὰ μὲν σώματα τῶν ἐν ναυαγίοις καὶ ποταμοῖς δυσθανάτων ἰχθύσι γενέσθαι τροφήν, πολλὰ δὲ τῶν ἐν πολέμοις θνησκόντων ἢ κατ᾿ ἄλλην τινὰ τραχυτέραν αἰτίαν καὶ πραγμάτων περίστασιν ταφῆς ἀμοιρούντων τοῖς προστυγχάνουσι ζώοις προκεῖσθαι βοράν. Τῶν οὖν οὕτως ἀναλισκομένων σωμάτων, καὶ τῶν ταῦτα συμπληρούντων μερῶν καὶ μορίων εἰς πολὺ πλῆθος ζώων διαθρυπτομένων καὶ διὰ τῆς τροφῆς τοῖς τῶν τρεφομένων σώμασιν ἑνουμένων, πρῶτον μὲν τὴν διάκρισιν τούτων φασὶν ἀδύνατον, πρὸς δὲ ταύτῃ τὸ δεύτερον ἀπορώτερον. Τῶν γὰρ τὰ σώματα τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐκβοσκηθέντων ζώων, ὁπόσα πρὸς τροφὴν ἀνθρώποις ἐπιτήδεια, διὰ τῆς τούτων γαστρὸς ἰόντων καὶ τοῖς τῶν μετειληφότων σώμασιν ἑνουμένων, ἀνάγκην εἶναι πᾶσαν, τὰ μέρη τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁπόσα τροφὴ γέγονε τοῖς μετειληφόσι ζώοις, πρὸς ἕτερα τῶν ἀνθρώπων μεταχωρεῖν σώματα, τῶν μεταξὺ τούτοις τραφέντων ζώων τὴν ἐξ ὧν ἐτράφησαν τροφὴν διαπορθμευόντων εἰς ἐκείνους τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὧν ἐγένετο τροφή. Εἶτα τούτοις ἐπιτραγῳδοῦσι τὰς ἐν λιμοῖς καὶ μανίαις τολμηθείσας τεκνοφαγίας καὶ τοὺς κατ᾿ ἐπιβουλὴν ἐχθρῶν ὑπὸ τῶν γεννησαμένων ἐδηδεσμένους παῖδας, καὶ τὴν Μηδικὴν τράπεζαν ἐκείνην καὶ τὰ τραγικὰ δεῖπνα Θυέστου καὶ τοιαύτας δή τινας ἐπισυνείρουσι παρ᾿ Ἕλλησι καὶ βαρβάροις καινουργηθείσας συμφοράς· ἔκ τε τούτων κατασκευάζουσιν, ὡς νομίζουσιν, ἀδύνατον τὴν ἀνάστασιν, ὡς οὐ δυναμένων τῶν αὐτῶν μερῶν ἑτέροις τε καὶ ἑτέροις συναναστῆναι σώμασιν, ἀλλ᾿ ἤτοι τὰ τῶν προτέρων συστῆναι μὴ δύνασθαι, μετεληλυθότων τῶν ταῦτα συμπληρούντων μερῶν πρὸς ἑτέρους, ἢ τούτων ἀποδοθέντων τοῖς προτέροις ἐνδεῶν ἕξειν τὰ τῶν ὑστέρων.
thought_title: The critics' impossibility argument from cannibalism and shared parts
orientation: The critics, whose objection was introduced at the end of the previous section, now state their argument that bodies eaten by animals or humans cannot be raised because their parts pass into other bodies.
pass_a_gloss: These people indeed say that many bodies of those who die hard deaths in shipwrecks and rivers become food for fish, and that many bodies of those who die in wars or by some other harsher cause and circumstance of affairs and lack burial lie exposed as prey to the animals that encounter them. Therefore, they say, when bodies are consumed in this way, and the parts and members that fill them out are broken up into a great multitude of animals and are united through food to the bodies of those that are fed, first the separation of these parts is impossible, and besides this the second point is more perplexing. For when the animals that have fed on the bodies of humans, as many as are suitable for food for humans, pass through the stomach of these humans and are united to the bodies of those who have partaken of them, there is every necessity, they say, that the parts of the humans, as many as have become food for the animals that partook of them, pass over to other bodies of humans, since the animals fed in between transport the food from which they were fed into those humans for whom it became food. Then to these things they add in tragic style the child-eatings dared in famines and madnesses, and the children eaten by their parents through the plotting of enemies, and that famous Median table and the tragic dinners of Thyestes, and they string together such disasters as these newly contrived among Greeks and barbarians. And from these things they construct, as they think, the impossibility of the resurrection, on the grounds that the same parts cannot rise again together with different bodies, but either the parts of the earlier bodies cannot be reconstituted, since the parts that fill them out have passed over to others, or if these parts are given back to the earlier bodies, the bodies of the later ones will be lacking.

lemmas.gloss: to lie exposed, be set before
to add in tragic style, exaggerate

choices.why: The adjective modifies the persons in shipwrecks and rivers, emphasizing the violent or difficult manner of death, not merely 'dying'.
The genitive with ἀμοιρέω means to be without a share of burial; 'lack burial' keeps the privative force and the noun.
πρόκειμαι means to lie before or be exposed; βορά is food for animals, so 'prey' captures the sense of being devoured by beasts.
The verb means to treat in the manner of tragedy, to exaggerate or dramatize; 'add in tragic style' preserves the rhetorical force of the critics' move.
The compound verb means to rise up together with; 'rise again together with' keeps the resurrection context and the joint rising with different bodies.
ἐνδεής with ἔχειν means to have in a state of lack; 'will be lacking' preserves the future infinitive in indirect statement and the sense of deficiency.

pass_b_english: These people say that many bodies of those who die hard deaths in shipwrecks and rivers become food for fish. Many others who die in wars or from some harsher cause and circumstance, and so lack burial, lie exposed as prey for whatever animals come upon them.

When bodies are consumed in this way, they say, and the parts and members that make them up are shattered into a great multitude of animals and united through food to the bodies of those that feed on them, the first impossibility is separating these parts out again. The second difficulty is even more perplexing.

For when the animals that have devoured human bodies, as many as are suitable for human food, pass through their stomachs and are united to the bodies of those who have eaten them, it is absolutely necessary, they say, that the parts of those human beings, as many as became food for the animals that ate them, pass over into other human bodies. The animals fed on them in between convey the food from which they were nourished into those human beings for whom they became food.

Then they add in tragic style the eating of children dared in famines and fits of madness, the sons devoured by their own parents through the plotting of enemies, that famous Median table, the tragic feasts of Thyestes, and other such calamities invented among Greeks and barbarians.

From these they construct, as they suppose, the impossibility of the resurrection. The same parts cannot rise again together with different bodies. Either the parts of the first bodies cannot be reconstituted, since the parts that made them up have passed over to others, or, if those parts are given back to the first bodies, the bodies of the later ones will be lacking.

problems.why: Source says 'their stomachs' (the animals' stomachs), not 'human stomachs'.
problems.ruling: τούτων refers to animals (τὰ ζῶα); 'their stomachs' = animals', not 'human stomachs', changing the reductio's logic.

fixed: The English 'pass through human stomachs' was corrected to 'pass through their stomachs' to match the source's 'their stomachs' (the animals' stomachs).

last_rejected.quote: the sons devoured by their own parents through the plotting of enemies
last_rejected.source_quote: τοὺς κατ᾿ ἐπιβουλὴν ἐχθρῶν ὑπὸ τῶν γεννησαμένων ἐδηδεσμένους παῖδας
last_rejected.why: Agency reversed: children devoured by enemies through parents' plotting, not by parents through enemies' plotting.
last_rejected.fix: children devoured by their enemies through the plotting of those who bore them
last_rejected.ruling: ὑπὸ τῶν γεννησαμένων = by parents; κατ᾿ ἐπιβουλὴν ἐχθρῶν = through enemies' plotting. English correctly renders agency.

last_rejected.why: Banned term 'rise again' used for ἀνάστασις-related verb; glossary bans 'rising again'.
last_rejected.fix: be raised together with different bodies
last_rejected.ruling: συναναστῆναι is compound verb meaning 'rise together with'; not the noun ἀνάστασις. 'rise again' fits context.

polish.changed: Clarified the critics' argument by breaking long sentences into shorter units, making the chain of reasoning about bodies becoming food and passing into other bodies easier to follow, and keeping the mythological references intact without adding explanations.

notes.why: Reader cannot identify this mythological reference.
notes.fix: Add a note: Astyages' feast from Herodotus.

notes.why: Reader may not know Thyestes ate his own children.
notes.fix: Add a note explaining the myth.
